solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Harvester's absence from work not welcome

definitions.note: the possessive reads as 'a harvester's tool', the curved blade used to cut crops

indicators.note: 'not' tells us the welcome is to be left out of the longer phrase

parts.note: time off when ill is sick leave
AVE is the Latin greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: A farmhand's day off is greeted with displeasure by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not welcome' strips AVE (Latin 'hail') from SICK LEAVE, leaving the reaping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvester traditionally reaps with this curved hand blade, so it is the harvester's implement.

clue.text: Feature of Bonneville, where old sailor lives?

definitions.meaning: Bonneville in Utah is a vast dried salt lakebed used for land speed records
an old sailor is a salt, and a flat is a home, so it is a salt's flat

explanation.definitionFit: The Bonneville Speedway runs across a dry salt-crusted plain; whimsically, a seadog's apartment.

clue.text: Item at end of sonnet

parts.note: an item is a romantic couple

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of sonnet

explanation.surface: A literary note on what closes a sonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' in the sense of two people going out together; the whole clue then describes the rhyming pair that closes a Shakespearean sonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean sonnet ends on a rhyming pair of lines, the final two-line unit.

clue.text: Clubs open attraction to make money

indicators.note: open here means the enticement word is split apart to admit a letter

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A sports club opens a new attraction as a money-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with a hint of greed, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Son tucked into mushroom after duck that's out of date

indicators.note: 'after duck' puts the fungus piece behind the O

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: tucked into means the son letter is pushed inside the fungus word

parts.note: a bolete is a mushroom with pores instead of gills

explanation.surface: A boy sits down to a mushroom dish after eating duck, a menu long out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' puts S inside BOLETE, a pored mushroom, just after its B; 'after duck' sets the whole behind O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is no longer in use, superseded and outmoded.

clue.text: What poor strings do makes you cringe

definitions.meaning: poor string players ... their instruments, sawing harshly
to cringe is to grovel obsequiously

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to behave servilely, and literally describes scratchy violin playing.

clue.text: Dish copper stud mounted in old firm

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the old and firm letters

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: mounted means climbing up, so in a down entry the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a boss is a stud or raised ornament

explanation.surface: A dish of copper with a raised stud, displayed in an old company.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounted' means read upwards; 'stud' is the ornamental boss, not a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Osso bucco is a Milanese dish of braised veal shanks.

clue.text: Food left beside battered cans

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so these seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food is left next to dented tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' looks like a link word but is fodder: 'battered' rearranges L plus BESIDE, and 'cans' ties wordplay to definition as 'is able to make'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fit to eat are foodstuffs, a plural noun for comestibles.

clue.text: Madrid article defends VIP as Crown Protector

indicators.note: defends here means surrounds and guards the celebrity word

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article, 'the'
a big name is a VIP, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A Spanish newspaper article champions a royal guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' is the dental sense, not the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer layer covers and guards the crown of a tooth.

clue.text: Throw a meal outdoors

indicators.note: outdoors reads as 'out of doors', the meal word standing outside the little a

parts.note: lunch is the midday meal

explanation.surface: An invitation to hold a picnic: throw a meal in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outdoors' puts LUNCH around A. 'Throw' as in hosting a party is the decoy; here it means hurl.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to throw or hurl it forcefully.

clue.text: What used to be on special kit carried by Sturmabteilung

definitions.text: What used to be on special kit carried by Sturmabteilung

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the abbreviation for the Nazi paramilitary

parts.note: SA is the usual abbreviation for the Sturmabteilung, the Nazi Brownshirts
past tense of 'is' gives was

indicators.note: special as in specially made, so the three letters of kit are reworked

explanation.surface: A historical note on the insignia that once appeared on the Brownshirts' uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the armband emblem the Brownshirts wore, so it works as an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked-cross emblem was worn on the uniform armbands of the Nazi Brownshirt militia.

clue.text: Store keen to stock wood with vehicle

indicators.note: to stock means to hold within, so the wailing word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
ash is a tree and its timber
and means with, as in bread and butter
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A shop is eager to stock timber along with a van for deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' is the verb meaning to wail, CRY, not eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesale warehouse where traders pay on the spot and take goods away themselves.

clue.text: Crawl over dales, distraught when promise is unfulfilled

indicators.note: over here means covering, the grovelling word wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: to fawn is to crawl or grovel to someone

indicators.note: distraught means upset and in disorder, so the letters of dales are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone creeps across the Yorkshire Dales in despair after being let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawl' looks like a verb of movement over the dales, but it is grovelling; 'over' means covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an early hopeful sign that comes to nothing, like light before sunrise that fades.

clue.text: I'm involved with this battle site in Belgium

indicators.note: involved means mixed up together, so the answer and I'm combine to rearrange into the country name

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have fought at this Belgian battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer's letters plus I'M, rearranged ('involved'), give BELGIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of the Bulge was fought in the Ardennes in 1944-45, so the place names a battle.

clue.text: He looks heavenwards when cup is returned to box

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a cup is a trophy

indicators.note: returned means the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: a cist is an ancient stone burial box or chest

explanation.surface: A sports winner sends the trophy back to its box and gazes skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes IS into SI. A CIST is a prehistoric stone coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies stars and galaxies, so their gaze is on the sky.

clue.text: Haunting old boy sings badly, swallowing tablets

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: swallowing means taking the drug letters inside the jumbled word
badly means poorly done, so the letters of sings are muddled

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: A former pupil, singing off-key after popping pills, is a haunting sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablets' is the crossword convention Es for ecstasy pills, placed after the first letter of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsessing you preoccupies and haunts your thoughts.

clue.text: Barn owl interpreted echo as something to drink

indicators.note: interpreted means rendered in another form, so the bird's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Echo is the radio alphabet code word for E

explanation.surface: A barn owl's hoot was taken to be an echo.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark, sweetish beer is a drink served in British pubs.

clue.text: Pens of warriors designed for them?

definitions.text: Pens of warriors designed for them?

indicators.note: designed means newly arranged to a plan, so those letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Enclosures for fighters built to house them: a camp for captured soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue, rearranged by 'designed', gives the answer, and it also describes POW camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Captured soldiers are held in pens, camps built for them, so the clue both builds and describes them.

clue.text: Ordinary seamen viewing figures

definitions.meaning: in the Royal Navy, non-commissioned sailors are called ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both naval sailors below officer rank and audience measurements for broadcasts.

clue.text: Various bits occupying tiny pages here

indicators.note: occupying means filling the space inside the small word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: various suggests a varied mixture, so the letters of bits are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Assorted fragments fill these tiny pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiny' is Scots wee; 'pages here' points to where web pages live.
explanation.definitionFit: Online pages are grouped together at an internet address, where you find them.

clue.text: Protein surplus approaching European margins

indicators.note: approaching places the surplus word just ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a glut is an excess or surplus

indicators.note: margins means the outside letters of European

explanation.surface: A report about Europe's excess protein production.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

clue.text: Many cherish origin of Ulster lily

indicators.note: to cherish is to hold close, so the plenty word embraces the letter

parts.note: lots means many

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of Ulster

explanation.surface: Many Northern Irish people hold dear the native lily of Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: The water plant is often called the water lily or sacred lily of the East.

clue.text: Source of love's arrow that's alluringly made up

definitions.meaning: the bow of the Roman god of love shoots his arrows
the double curve of the upper lip, often emphasised with lipstick for allure

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the god Cupid's archery bow; figuratively the curved upper lip line accentuated with make-up.

clue.text: Pasta ingredient university kept in barrel

indicators.note: kept in means the letter is stored inside the container word

parts.note: a drum is a barrel-shaped container

explanation.surface: A college stores its pasta flour in a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is the hard wheat whose semolina is used to make pasta.

clue.text: More pungent special port

parts.note: tangier means having a sharper taste or smell

explanation.surface: A smelly special harbour, perhaps fish and spice markets.
explanation.walkthrough: TANGIERS is an older English spelling of Tangier, the Moroccan port.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is the seaport city on Morocco's Strait of Gibraltar coast.

clue.text: Bruised crania? This is said to help

definitions.text: Bruised crania? This is said to help

indicators.note: bruised means battered out of shape, so the letters of crania are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knock on the head? This remedy is supposed to ease it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the herbal cream rubbed on bruises; 'said to' hints its benefit is unproven.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain plant is used in creams and ointments claimed to soothe bruising.

clue.text: Posies one's arranged? They're not straight

indicators.note: arranged as flowers are arranged, the four letters put in a new order

parts.note: the letters of one's without its apostrophe
gays are people who are not straight, i.e. not heterosexual

explanation.surface: Someone arranges small bouquets and notices the stems are all bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bunches of fragrant flowers are both called posies and nosegays.

clue.text: Limped everywhere, hiding shackle

indicators.note: hiding means the answer is concealed within the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A prisoner hobbled everywhere, concealing his leg irons.
explanation.definitionFit: To shackle someone is to hamper or hinder their movement, like a verb meaning hinder.
